reasons: Lake identity identifies the case as Adams v. Williams, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1972-06-12, year 1972.
Lake citations list official citation 407 U.S. 143, parallel citations 92 S. Ct. 1921 and 32 L. Ed. 2d 612, and vendor-neutral citation 1972 U.S. LEXIS 2206.
The opinion rejects the argument that reasonable cause for stop and frisk can only rest on the officer's personal observation.
The opinion states that informants' tips vary in reliability and may justify police response when sufficiently reliable, making the Reasonable Suspicion home relation supportable.
residual_risks: The role label is topical metadata, not a holding stated verbatim by the court.

reasons: The opinion says the informant was known personally, had provided information before, came forward personally, gave immediately verifiable information, and that the information carried enough indicia of reliability to justify the forcible stop.
The opinion expressly rejects limiting stop-and-frisk reasonable cause to the officer's own personal observations.
The opinion holds the reach to the reported gun location was a reasonable limited protective intrusion.
residual_risks: The short holding should not be read to make every known face-to-face tip sufficient without the reliability facts present in Adams.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Consider adding that the tip was specific, immediately verifiable, from an informant known personally and previously used, and involved a reported gun at Williams's waist.

reasons: The opinion frames the case as applying Terry and concludes the police action conformed to Terry's standards.
Adams applies Terry to an informant-tip stop and protective weapons search, supporting a Progeny role for Terry Stops and Reasonable Suspicion.
Lake identity lists court_level as scotus and court as U.S. Supreme Court, supporting the authority-weight label Binding — SCOTUS.
No treatment/currency defect is raised under Lens A.
residual_risks: Treatment and currency are outside Lens A review.
